# Discussion Board Project Overview and Objectives

## Overview
The Discussion Board is designed as a dedicated online platform for in-depth political and economic discussion, setting itself apart from conventional forums through intentional community design, moderation excellence, and a commitment to discussion quality. Unlike general-purpose boards, this forum targets users such as policy enthusiasts, academics, students, professionals, and members of the public who seek constructive debate on complex national and international issues. Its moderation philosophy is rooted in balancing open dialogue with community welfare: moderators are empowered not just to remove harmful or off-topic posts, but to actively foster a climate where evidence-based arguments, respectful disagreement, and diversity of perspectives are valued. The platform will incorporate rigorous content flagging, transparent moderation logs, clear community guidelines, and feedback loops to ensure optimum discussion quality. "High-quality discussion" is defined not only by civility, but by the prevalence of well-reasoned, well-sourced contributions and the minimization of personal attacks, misinformation, or echo chambers. 

## Vision
Our vision is to become the premier digital space for informed and meaningful debate in political and economic domains. We aim to address the challenges of polarization, the spread of misinformation, trolling, and the often hostile environments found on competing platforms. The Discussion Board's core values—integrity, transparency, and inclusiveness—are demonstrated through features such as public moderation logs, statistical reporting on flagged content, inclusive onboarding for new voices, and technical measures against bots and shills. Concrete targets include: a 90% user satisfaction rate regarding fairness of moderation; a <5% prevalence of reported misinformation on trending threads (as verified by fact-checking); and measurable diversity in users' backgrounds and viewpoints. The platform strives for a reputation where users trust the reliability, openness, and fairness of discourse, supported by systems that reward constructive engagement and the elevation of underrepresented perspectives.

## Business Goals
- **Foster a Vibrant Community**: Achieve sustained daily participation of 5,000+ engaged members within 12 months. Example initiatives include topic-of-the-week contests and expert AMAs. Metrics: DAU/MAU, new post volume, and retention rates.
- **Ensure High-Quality Dialogue**: Implement incentive systems for upvoted, well-researched posts, such as recognition badges and access to premium features. Projected outcome: 70% of threads surpass a discussion quality threshold (measured via peer review and moderator scoring).
- **Monetize Responsibly**: Offer optional paid memberships granting access to exclusive reports, ad-free browsing, and advanced analytics, aiming for a 3%+ conversion rate by end of year one. Metrics: MRR, user upgrade rate, churn analysis.
- **Safeguard Security & Compliance**: Establish GDPR-compliant data policies with regular audits and user-friendly consent tools. Track: zero reportable data incidents per year, positive user security perception surveys.

## Core Objectives
- **Promote Constructive Dialogue**: Encourage practices such as citing sources, using structured arguments, and refraining from personal attacks. Employ behavioral guidelines and visible incentives (e.g., badges for civil discourse) with AI-assisted moderation support to recognize and highlight exemplary contributions.
- **Maintain Platform Integrity & Trust**: Instill robust mechanisms against manipulation (e.g., coordinated inauthentic behavior, astroturfing), regular disclosure of moderation actions, and a user reputation system. Objective: cultivate trust through visible accountability and open feedback.
- **Prioritize Robust Security & Data Governance**: Use state-of-the-art encryption, strict access control, and secure audit trails for all sensitive operations. Ensure users can manage their privacy preferences easily and transparently. Regularly review systems for vulnerabilities, maintaining compliance with all applicable legal standards.

## Discussion Board User Roles and Permissions
This section will provide a detailed breakdown of all user types and their associated permissions, mapped directly to system authentication and authorization protocols. It will define what regular members, moderators, and admins can do, supported by scenarios such as posting, editing, moderating, and accessing configuration settings. This enables clarity for developers implementing role-based access controls and supports transparency for all users regarding platform governance.

# 02. Discussion Board – User Roles and Permissions

## Overview
This document provides a comprehensive definition of user roles, their permissions, and responsibilities within the Discussion Board system. Clearly establishing these roles ensures consistent API authentication, robust access control, and lays the foundation for both secure and efficient operations. The system supports a multi-tiered user model tailored to foster open yet moderated discussions on political and economic topics.

## Roles Definition
The three principal roles are: **member**, **moderator**, and **admin**. Each role is tied to specific authentication scopes and operational boundaries.

### 1. Member
**Description**: General registered users engaging in discussions.
- **Authentication Requirement**: Must register and verify via API (email, password).
- **Core Permissions**:
  - View, create, and edit own posts and comments
  - Participate in voting or reacting to posts if enabled
  - Report inappropriate content to moderators
  - Manage own profile and settings
- **Restrictions**: Cannot access moderation tools or system settings

### 2. Moderator
**Description**: Trusted users assigned to maintain community standards.
- **Authentication Requirement**: Elevated credentials (granted by admin) with two-factor authentication recommended
- **Core Permissions**:
  - All member permissions
  - Edit or remove posts/comments violating guidelines
  - Review and resolve reports of inappropriate content
  - Warn or temporarily suspend members within grounds
  - Access moderation dashboard, log actions
- **Restrictions**: Cannot manage system configuration or user roles outside moderation scope

### 3. Admin
**Description**: Superuser responsible for complete oversight and system operation.
- **Authentication Requirement**: Highest credential (must enforce strong password and 2FA)
- **Core Permissions**:
  - All moderator permissions
  - Create, modify, or delete user roles (including assigning moderators)
  - Manage user accounts (activate, deactivate, or permanently ban)
  - Configure forum structure, global system settings, and integrations
  - View system-wide reports and analytics

## Permission Matrix
| Permission / Action                              | Member | Moderator | Admin    |
|-------------------------------------------------|--------|-----------|----------|
| View posts / comments                           |   ✓    |    ✓      |    ✓     |
| Create posts / comments                         |   ✓    |    ✓      |    ✓     |
| Edit own posts / comments                       |   ✓    |    ✓      |    ✓     |
| Delete own posts / comments                     |   ✓    |    ✓      |    ✓     |
| Report content                                  |   ✓    |    ✓      |    ✓     |
| Edit/delete any post/comment                    |        |    ✓      |    ✓     |
| Access moderation dashboard                     |        |    ✓      |    ✓     |
| Warn/suspend users                              |        |    ✓      |    ✓     |
| Review/resolve reports                          |        |    ✓      |    ✓     |
| Manage user accounts (ban, deactivate, etc.)    |        |           |    ✓     |
| Configure system/settings/roles                 |        |           |    ✓     |
| Manage forum categories and topics              |        |           |    ✓     |
| Access system analytics and logs                |        |           |    ✓     |

## API Authentication Scopes
- **member**: Tokens allow posting, commenting, editing own content, and reporting; limited to personal data endpoints.
- **moderator**: Tokens allow additional access to moderation endpoints: review, edit, delete, and reporting dashboards.
- **admin**: Full API access, including all user management, configuration, and sensitive operations. Multi-factor authentication is enforced for all privileged operations.

## Role Escalation & Management
- Only admins may assign or revoke moderator privileges.
- Moderator and admin actions are recorded in the audit log.
- Role changes are communicated to affected users (e.g., via email or system notification).

## Security Considerations
- Enforce least privilege: users should have only the permissions necessary for their function.
- Periodically review roles and entitlements to detect and mitigate privilege creep.
- Strong authentication and logging for all moderator and admin activities.

See the [Table of Contents](./00_DiscussionBoard_Table_of_Contents.md) for related documentation and navigation.

# Discussion Board: User Journeys and Workflows

## Overview
This document outlines the core user journeys and system workflows for the Discussion Board platform, enabling structured participation around political and economic topics. The journeys are mapped to three primary roles: member, moderator, and admin. Each role's activities are described through key scenarios that reflect common user goals and operational requirements.

---

## 1. Member Journeys

### 1.1 Registration and Access
- **Account Creation**: Member visits registration page, provides email, password, and agrees to terms. Upon successful verification, member gains access.
- **Login/Logout**: Secure authentication via email and password. Session is maintained until logout or inactivity timeout.

### 1.2 Browsing and Discovering Topics
- Members access the forum homepage, viewing a categorized list of political and economic discussion boards.
- Filtering and search tools enable quick navigation to topics of interest.

### 1.3 Creating and Participating in Discussions
- **Post Topic**: Member selects a category, creates a new thread by submitting a title and body, optionally attaching files.
- **View Details**: Member clicks into topics to see full posts, comments, and participant activity.
- **Comment/Reply**: Members submit comments or reply to existing comments, building threaded discussions.
- **Edit/Delete Own Content**: Members can modify or delete their own posts/comments within editable periods.

### 1.4 Engagement
- **Voting/Liking**: Optionally, members can upvote, like, or react to posts/comments.
- **Reporting**: Members report inappropriate content using an in-post/report button, flagging for moderation review.


## 2. Moderator Workflows

### 2.1 Monitoring Activity
- Moderators review new posts, comments, and reports from the member community using dashboards and notification tools.

### 2.2 Content Moderation
- **Approve/Reject Posts and Comments**: Moderators validate content for rule compliance, removing or editing as needed.
- **Issue Warnings/Bans**: When violations occur, moderators may warn users or suspend accounts, following escalation protocols.
- **Handle Reports**: For each reported item, moderators review the case, log actions taken, and update report statuses.

### 2.3 Communication
- Via announcements or direct messages, moderators notify members of actions taken or policy updates.


## 3. Admin Workflows

### 3.1 Forum and User Management
- **User Administration**: Admins view, edit, or remove any user account, assign or revoke moderator privileges.
- **Category/Board Setup**: Create, update, or delete boards and topic categories.

### 3.2 Configuration and Settings
- Manage system-wide settings, permissions, feature flags, and community guidelines.
- Review system/usage analytics and audit logs for governance.

---

## 4. Workflow Diagrams

### Member Content Contribution
```mermaid
graph TD;
    A[Start] --> B(Login/Register);
    B --> C[Browse Boards];
    C --> D[Create Post or Comment];
    D --> E[Engage (Vote/Report)];
    E --> F[Logout/Session End];
```

### Moderation Issue Resolution
```mermaid
graph TD;
    M1[Moderator Receives Report] --> M2[Review Content];
    M2 --> M3{Violation?};
    M3 -- Yes --> M4[Edit/Delete Content];
    M3 -- No --> M5[Dismiss/Close Report];
    M4 --> M6[Notify User];
    M6 --> M7[Document Outcome];
    M5 --> M7;
```

### Administrative Oversight
```mermaid
graph TD;
    A1[Admin Login] --> A2[Review System Analytics];
    A2 --> A3[Manage Users & Forums];
    A3 --> A4[Update Settings];
    A4 --> A5[Logout/Session End];
```

---

## 5. Key Scenario Table

| Role       | Scenario                      | Entry Point            | Completion    |
|------------|------------------------------|------------------------|---------------|
| Member     | Create a Topic                | Board list             | Topic posted  |
| Member     | Comment on Topic              | Topic details          | Comment saved |
| Member     | Report Content                | Post/comment options   | Report filed  |
| Moderator  | Review Report                 | Moderator dashboard    | Action taken  |
| Admin      | Add New Category              | Admin panel            | Category live |

---

## 6. Summary
This document details the main journeys and operational flows central to fostering a vibrant, well-moderated, and user-driven discussion platform. These workflows empower each user role to contribute to a safe, organized, and dynamic community experience.

# Discussion Board: Requirements and Business Rules

## 1. Overview
This document details all core requirements and business rules for the political/economic discussion board platform. It is self-contained and supplies everything needed for effective development, validation, and future feature expansion.

## 2. Functional Requirements
### 2.1 User Registration & Authentication
- Users (members, moderators, admins) must be able to register and authenticate using secure mechanisms (email/password, optional 2FA).
- Only verified accounts gain access to posting and commenting functions.

### 2.2 User Roles & Permissions
- **Member:** Can create topics, post, comment, like/dislike, report inappropriate content.
- **Moderator:** Can perform all Member actions plus edit/delete any post/comment, resolve reports, and issue warnings or temporary suspensions.
- **Admin:** Full permissions, including user management, board structure configuration, analytics, and security setting adjustments.

### 2.3 Content Operations
- Users can create topics with a title, description, and tags.
- Posts and comments support markdown formatting and attachments (e.g., images, PDFs).
- Users can edit or delete their own posts/comments unless locked or under moderation.

### 2.4 Discussion Management
- Threads are chronologically and hierarchically organized (replies to comments supported).
- Voting (like/dislike) and flagging functions available for every post/comment.
- Hot topics and trending posts are algorithmically surfaced.

### 2.5 Moderation Features
- Reporting flow for inappropriate content, spam, or abuse.
- Moderators review flagged content, with required audit trail logging (actions, timestamps, moderator identity).
- Temporary or permanent user suspensions can be issued.

### 2.6 Notifications & Communication
- Users can opt-in for email or in-app notifications: replies, mentions, moderation updates, board announcements.

## 3. Non-Functional Requirements
- **Availability:** 99.5% uptime target (excluding scheduled maintenance).
- **Performance:** Response times under 1 second for main actions.
- **Scalability:** Support for bursts in user numbers, up to 10,000+ concurrent users.
- **Security:** All personal data encrypted in transit and at rest; regular security audits.
- **Accessibility:** WCAG 2.1 AA level compliance.

## 4. Business Rules
- Discussions must remain on political/economic topics; off-topic content can be removed or moved at moderator/admin discretion.
- Registered users must accept a Code of Conduct outlining respectful behavior, anti-harassment, and zero tolerance for hate speech.
- Each user can report up to 10 items of content per day to avoid abuse of the reporting system.
- Suspended users cannot post, comment, or vote; their prior posts remain unless deleted by a moderator or admin.
- Topic tags are curated; users can propose new tags, but moderator/admin approval is required.
- Automated filters mask profanity and flag suspected spam before publication, pending moderator review.
- Data retention: all posts and logs retained for a minimum of 2 years for legal and audit requirements.

## 5. Future Considerations
- Integration with external authentication providers (OAuth, SSO).
- Advanced analytics for post engagement, user activity heatmaps.
- Support for live events, video debates, and scheduled panel discussions.
- Multilingual support for non-English discussions subject to moderation resourcing.

## 6. Acceptance Criteria
- All listed role permissions are enforced at the API, backend, and UI layers.
- Moderation and audit logs are immutable and accessible only to administrators.
- Functional tests cover all user journeys: registration, posting, reporting, moderation, and notification flows.

---
**End of Document.**

models.name: discussionboard_channels
models.description:
Discussion Board Channels - This implements the requirement for multi-channel/forum environments from the original business requirements (see 04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md Section 2.3, 2.4). 

Channel represents a top-level grouping for boards/forums for both scalability and community segmentation. Maintains 3NF normalization by separating channel metadata from board or topic-specific data. For example, a platform with 'Politics', 'Economics', and 'International Relations' channels allows targeted thread organization and user permissions per channel.

Key relationships: referenced by boards in other domains (not directly here). 
Special behaviors: Disabling a channel hides all associated boards and content without deletion.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique channel identifier.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Channel code - Implements unique channel identifier for internal reference. Example: 'POLI', 'ECON'. Ensures normalization by providing atomic lookup field without duplication. Usage: for routing and analytics.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Human-readable channel name - Implements user interface representation. Example: 'Politics', 'Economics'. Keeps display values separate from codes for flexibility.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Extended channel description - For longer UI help text or onboarding popups. Atomic, nullable for optional UX.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: Channel enabled status - Indicates whether this channel is active and visible to users. Fulfills configurability requirement without hard deletion.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp - When the channel was first created. Supports auditability, required for 3NF and not derived.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp - When channel metadata was last changed. Supports audit trails and user interface freshness.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp - Implements business rule: channels never hard-deleted, are flagged for removal. If null, not deleted; if set, should not be shown to users.

models.name: discussionboard_categories
models.description:
Discussion Board Categories - This supports hierarchical topic grouping within channels, directly mapping to the business requirement for organized board structuring from 03_DiscussionBoard_User_Journeys_and_Workflows.md and 04_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md (section 2.3, 2.4). 

Category allows grouping boards for navigational clarity and thematic relevance. Maintains 3NF normalization by atomically storing categories separate from boards or topics. Example: categories like 'International', 'Domestic', 'Elections', under a 'Politics' channel.

Key relationships: often referenced by boards (in other files); can support parent-child via 'parent_id' field if hierarchy is desired.
Special behaviors: Disabling a category hides its boards/topics from users but retains data.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique category identifier.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_channel_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged channel's {@link discussionboard_channels.id} - Associates the category with its parent channel, ensuring each category is correctly placed in the forum hierarchy. Enforces normalization by separating channel from category business logic.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Optional parent category's {@link discussionboard_categories.id} - Enables category nesting for themes/subcategories. Null when top-level; fulfills 3NF by storing hierarchy atomically.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Category code - Atomic, unambiguous handle for programmatic reference. E.g., 'ELECTIONS'. Maintains normalization and allows unique lookups.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category name - Display string for UI, supports search and multilingual use. Atomic, not derived.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Long category description - For help popups, onboarding, or detailed UI. Nullable, kept atomic for 3NF.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: Category enabled state - Fulfills admin business rule for soft-hiding categories without data loss.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp - For audit/logging, non-derived.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Update timestamp - Last metadata modification. Maintains full normalization and is not derived.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp - Category is hidden, not deleted. 3NF compliant, nullable for full retention/audit support.

models.name: discussionboard_settings
models.description:
Discussion Board Global Settings - Implements central configuration management as required in business rules (see 04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md Section 2.6 and 3). 

Allows admin and system-wide settings to be referenced from code and API. All settings are atomic key-value pairs, fully normalized (no pre-calculated aggregates). For example: spam filter thresholds, maintenance modes, global flags. This model is NOT used for user-specific settings (those are in other components).

Key relationships: None (standalone configuration repository).
Special behaviors: Only admin users can modify; changes are logged in the audit records.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique configuration setting row.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Setting key - Atomic string, namespaced for collision avoidance. E.g., 'maintenance_mode', 'email:smtp_host'. Fulfills 3NF by logically separating individual settings.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Setting value - Actual config data, stored as string for flexibility (booleans stored as 'true'/'false', numbers as strings, etc.). Remains atomic and is not calculated/derived.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Description of this setting - Used for admin UI and inline documentation. Nullable for flexibility. Maintains 3NF by separating metadata.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when setting was first added. Fulfills audit/history requirement.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last modification for tracking. Business use: rollback or troubleshooting.

models.name: discussionboard_audit_logs
models.description:
Discussion Board System Audit Trail - Implements mandatory audit logging (see 04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md Section 2.5, 4, 6). 

Captures all system-critical and admin/moderator actions for legal compliance, accountability, and troubleshooting. Maintains 3NF by separating each log entry as an atomic event record. Usage example: records when an admin changes a setting, a moderator deletes content, or a user is suspended. Read-only unless system/admin privilege.

Key relationships: References acting user in other actor components (not handled here).
Special behaviors: Entries are immutable and must not be modified/deleted except by hard data retention policies.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique audit log entry.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: Audit action description - Atomic, non-derived string classifying the action (e.g., 'SETTING_UPDATE', 'ACCOUNT_SUSPEND'). Fully normalized: each event is one row. Examples: 'BOARD_CREATE', 'POST_DELETE', 'WARNING_ISSUED'.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: ID of user performing the action - Cross-references actors (members, moderators, admins) in other domains. Fulfills audit traceability requirement by unambiguously linking log to user. This is NOT a foreign key to allow for actor deletion scenarios.

plainFields.name: target_table
plainFields.description: Target table/entity affected - Describes what system entity was changed (e.g., 'discussionboard_boards', 'discussionboard_threads'). Key for traceability and reporting.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: ID of affected entity - When applicable, stores the row/entity affected by the event. Separate from 'actor_id'. Nullable for actions like login, where there may be no entity affected.

plainFields.name: details
plainFields.description: Additional details - JSON string or extended data for complex actions (e.g., before/after snapshot). Fully atomic as business rule prohibits redundancy.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Audit entry creation timestamp - Required, non-derived, for every action (full audit compliance).

models.name: discussionboard_members
models.description:
Member entity for board platform - Implements actor/user identity core from the Actors domain and requirement sections (esp. Role & Registration).  

This models the base member user that can register, post, comment, and interact. Maintains full 3NF normalization—member preferences, authentications, roles, and profile are handled in related tables. Used when linking posts, comments, reports, notifications to a unique user identity.

Example usage: Track who authored a thread, likes a post, or receives a notification.

Key relationships: Links to profiles, authentications, suspensions, moderator/admin entities. 
Special behaviors: Member can only have one unique identity, unique email enforced at authentication level.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each member in the system.

plainFields.name: joined_at
plainFields.description: Member join date/time - Implements audit/tracking requirement. Indicates when the member registered. Ensures normalization by placing date in member (not profile) for clear audit. E.g. "2025-07-22T11:00:00+09:00".

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current member status - Implements business rules on activation/suspension. Values like 'active', 'pending', or 'suspended'. For example, initial status is 'active'; if suspended, some privileges are blocked; status field reflects business logic, not derived from suspension table.

models.name: discussionboard_moderators
models.description:
Moderator entity - Implements moderator elevation from requirements (Role & Permission, Moderation Workflows). 

Stores references to member IDs elevated as moderators. Maintains 3NF as separate table. E.g., a member can have a record here when promoted to moderator; demotion is soft by setting an end timestamp.

Key usage: Map member to moderator privileges, history, and actions.
Key relationships: Links to member, logs actions in discussionboard_moderator_actions.
Special behaviors: Only admins can add records; member cannot be moderator twice at the same time.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Link to the promoted member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Establishes which user is the moderator.

plainFields.name: promoted_at
plainFields.description: Datetime member became moderator. Implements audit and escalation requirement for privilege history.

plainFields.name: demoted_at
plainFields.description: Datetime moderator stopped being moderator. Null if currently holds role. Maintains audit trail; 3NF (not in member base table).

models.name: discussionboard_admins
models.description:
Admin entity - Implements admin user architecture per requirements. 

Records which members are elevated to admin status (system superuser). Keeps normalized; not merged with member or moderator. Usage: assign admin API permissions, log system config changes, etc.

Key relationships: FK to member. 
Special: Only unique for each member; admin may also be moderator.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Link to member who is admin. References {@link discussionboard_members.id}.

plainFields.name: elevated_at
plainFields.description: Datetime admin privilege granted; implements privilege audit. For example, assigned by platform owner.

models.name: discussionboard_member_profiles
models.description:
Member profile details - Implements requirements for profile management (user journeys, self-editable info, privacy compliance). 

Stores optional extended member info: display name, bio, links, avatar, etc. Strictly 3NF: profile data not mixed with authentication, roles, or business states.

Usage example: Display profile page; allow user edits; fulfill download-my-data requests.

Key relationships: Exists 0 or 1 per member, not required for minimal registration.
Special: All fields optional (nullable = true where privacy applies).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: FK to the owner member. References {@link discussionboard_members.id}.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Optional user-chosen display name. Implements flexible identity requirement, separate from authentication username, upholds normalization. E.g. "Jane D."

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Short biography field. Implements requirements for expressive/optional profile data; null if user left blank. 3NF; not mixed with system identity.

plainFields.name: avatar_uri
plainFields.description: Avatar image URI - Implements profile customization; URI to profile image if present. Upholds normalization: actual file stored in separate attachment table.

plainFields.name: website
plainFields.description: Personal website URI. Optional extra info; good for professional profiles. Nulls preserved for privacy. 3NF compliance (not in auth).

plainFields.name: location
plainFields.description: Optional location for user. Provides for geography-based statistics or voluntary self-disclosure; optional for privacy. 3NF (won’t be used for enforcement or regional rules).

models.name: discussionboard_member_authentications
models.description:
Member authentication methods - Implements secure credentials, multi-method login, and audit requirements. 

Stores hashed passwords, external ID references, last login timestamp, and auth tokens where needed. 3NF: authentication split into own table with FK to member. 

Usage: Support classic email/password, future-proof for SSO/OAuth extensions.

Relationships: Each member can have multiple credentials (for multi-provider login/fallback).
Security: No cleartext passwords; only hashed tokens or references. Unique per (provider, username/email).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: FK to member identity this credential belongs to. References {@link discussionboard_members.id}.

plainFields.name: provider
plainFields.description: Authentication provider e.g. 'local', 'google', 'kakao'. Implements requirement for flexible login. Used in uniqueness check.

plainFields.name: provider_identifier
plainFields.description: Provider-unique identity (e.g. email for local, user ID for external). Implements multi-method login and support for identification challenges.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hash of password or auth token (never cleartext). Null for OAuth-type logins (where external token not stored after exchange). Enforces security by avoiding password in main member table. 3NF compliance.

plainFields.name: last_login_at
plainFields.description: Last successful login datetime for credential. Implements auditing per security NFR.

models.name: discussionboard_member_suspensions
models.description:
Records member suspensions for rules enforcement (Moderation/Business Rules).

Represents suspending/blocking users temporarily or permanently. Tracks when, why, and by whom suspension was issued or revoked. 3NF—suspension details not mixed with member core or moderator/action logs.

Usage: Determine posting eligibility, fulfill 2-year audit retention (business rule). Suspension info drives API/feature gating.

Relationships: FK to member. Optionally records moderator/admin who issued/ended action.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: FK to affected member. Indicates who is/was suspended. References {@link discussionboard_members.id}.

foreignFields.name: issued_by_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: FK to moderator who issued suspension (if from moderator). References {@link discussionboard_moderators.id}. Null if action was admin only.

foreignFields.name: issued_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: FK to admin who issued suspension (if admin). References {@link discussionboard_admins.id}. Null if not admin action.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Suspension reason/notes. Implements business rule for tracking justification and fulfills audit requirement. E.g. 'Repeated off-topic posts'.

plainFields.name: starts_at
plainFields.description: Suspension start date/time. Implements gating logic (when member loses privileges). Upholds normalization (event data outside status field).

plainFields.name: ends_at
plainFields.description: Suspension end date/time (null if permanent/active). 3NF (not derived, always recorded as explicit field).

plainFields.name: revoked_at
plainFields.description: When (if ever) suspension was revoked/cancelled before scheduled end. Null if not revoked or full term served.

models.name: discussionboard_moderator_actions
models.description:
Moderator action logs for audit and transparency (Moderation & Business Rules). 

Stores immutable records of moderator intervention: edit, delete, warning, suspension, tag approval, etc. Implements requirements for transparency, reporting, and appeal/audit workflows. 

Strictly 3NF - action log is separated, not mixed with member core. Includes full details for future analytics and review.

Key relationships: FK to moderator who acted, affects other entities by reference. Used directly in admin dashboard, and for providing appeal evidence.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: FK to moderator who performed the action (must exist in moderator table). References {@link discussionboard_moderators.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of action performed (e.g. 'edit_post', 'delete_comment', 'issue_warning', 'suspend_member', 'approve_tag'). Implements business rule for clear log granularity and enables filtered reports. No calculation—just event type storage.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity affected (e.g. 'post', 'comment', 'member', 'tag'). Needed for correct log analysis and future extensibility.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: ID of target entity—may reference various tables depending on action_type/target_type. Implements need to audit what exact record was affected by an action. (No FK since polymorphic.)

plainFields.name: details
plainFields.description: Full description of action details, justification, or notes. Helps implement transparency & fulfill legal/audit/compliance requirements.

plainFields.name: action_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the action was taken. For reporting and workflow tracking.

models.name: discussionboard_boards
models.description:
Board definition entity - Implements section 2.3 Content Operations and 4. Business Rules, supporting organization of discussions by topic (e.g., 'Politics', 'Economics'). 

Business explanation: This table holds the definitions of all boards visible in the system, each representing a broad topical area. Fully normalized: each board is atomic with no denormalized or pre-calculated data. Example: 'Global Politics', 'Macroeconomics'.

Key relationships: May be referenced by board topics; may reference categories (from other components) for further organization. 
Special behaviors: Board codes must be unique.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the board entity.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_category_id
foreignFields.description: Parent category's {@link discussionboard_categories.id}. Organizes boards under broader discussion categories (category is managed by another domain).

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Board code - Implements unique identification for boards for routing and business logic. Example: 'POLITICS', 'ECONOMICS'. Ensures normalization; not derived from name. Usage: programmatic API references.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Board name - Implements display and search requirements. Used for UI listing. Normalized atomic field.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Board description - Implements business rule for onboarding and help text. Provides context to users. Example: 'Discuss current events and policy in global politics.'

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether the board is currently active and visible to users. Supports moderation/administrative workflows. Implements part of business rule for board visibility.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of board creation. Required for audit and governance. Used in onboarding and reporting. Not pre-calculated. Always present.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for the board. Enables tracking of administrative changes. Part of audit trail compliance.

models.name: discussionboard_board_topics
models.description:
Topics within each board - Implements section 2.3 Content Operations (thread creation) and logical separation of user-created conversations under boards.

Business explanation: Each topic is a user-defined thread for discussion within a specific board, such as 'Presidential Elections 2025'. Topics refer to boards and have atomic fields for normalization. Fully normalized; per-topic data only, no denormalized aggregates.

Key relationships: References discussionboard_boards as parent; referenced by threads (in another schema); references topic tags for categorization.
Special behaviors: Topic codes are unique per board; topics are never global.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the board topic entity.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_board_id
foreignFields.description: Parent board's {@link discussionboard_boards.id}. Organizes this topic within a board. Required association for business logic and enforcement of domain boundaries.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Topic code, unique per board - Implements unique identification for user-facing links or moderation. Example: 'ELECTIONS', 'Q4_OUTLOOK'.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Topic title - Implements user requirement for conversation subjects. Example: '2025 Presidential Elections Discussion'. Normalized atomic field.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Descriptive summary of the topic for onboarding/search. Example: 'A space to debate strategies, candidates, and international impact.'

plainFields.name: created_by_member_id
plainFields.description: Creator's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Reference to the member who created the topic. Implements functional requirement for traceability and audit.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp. Used for ordering and audit trails, required by audit and reporting requirements.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for the topic, for audit trail and modification control.

models.name: discussionboard_topic_tags
models.description:
Topic tag definitions - Implements requirement for curated, moderated topical tagging of discussions (see business rules section 4 and functional requirement 2.4).

Business explanation: Stores curated list of tags that can be assigned to topics, supporting search and categorization. Fully normalized - tags are atomic and not denormalized. Proposed tags managed elsewhere; this table is only for approved/curated tags.

Key relationships: Referenced by board topics or threads for categorization. 
Special behaviors: Uniqueness constraint on tag name; tags are not auto-accepted and require moderator/admin approval via separate processes.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the topic tag entity.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Tag name (unique) - Implements business rule for curated tags. Example: 'Elections', 'Policy', 'Economics'. Searchable and atomic for normalization.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether tag is enabled for assignment to topics or threads. Implements moderation requirement for hidden/disabled tags.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of tag creation - supports audit and governance. Always present.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last modification timestamp, supporting change tracking for moderation/audit.

models.name: discussionboard_board_announcements
models.description:
Moderator/admin announcement entity - Implements requirement 2.6 (Notifications & Communication), enabling information dissemination within boards.

Business explanation: Contains announcements or system messages linked to specific boards (e.g., rule updates, special events). Announcements are always linked to a board, have a title/body, and track who published them. Fully normalized, no denormalized aggregates. 

Key relationships: References discussionboard_boards, admin/moderator (publisher) via foreign keys. Referenced by notification logic in other components for in-app/email alerts.
Special behaviors: Soft deletion supported via deleted_at. Announcements must be orderable by creation timestamp.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the announcement.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_board_id
foreignFields.description: Target board's {@link discussionboard_boards.id}. All announcements are scoped to a specific board. Implements section 2.6 Notification flows.

foreignFields.name: published_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin/moderator's {@link discussionboard_admins.id} who published the announcement. Used for audit and permission control.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Announcement title - Implements requirement for concise notification. Example: 'Rule Change: Civility Policy Updated'.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Full message body - Implements detailed notification requirement. Markdown supported. Example: 'The board's civility policy has changed...'.

plainFields.name: is_pinned
plainFields.description: If true, announcement is 'sticky' on board; implements business rule for highlighting key messages. Only one active pin per board at a time (enforced in API logic).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp; enables ordering and audit trace.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last modification timestamp for tracking changes and audit.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp; if not null, announcement is hidden but not physically deleted (supports audit/legal retention).

models.name: discussionboard_threads
models.description:
Discussion Thread entity - This implements the foundational requirement for organizing topic-based discussions (see 04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md, 2.3, 2.4). 

Represents a top-level topic or conversation within a board, containing metadata about the origin, categorization, and lifecycle of the thread. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating threads from posts/comments and referencing users and boards via foreign keys only. For example, a thread initiates a new discussion about a political or economic topic, to which users may contribute posts and comments.

Key relationships: Relates to boards (discussionboard_boards) and users (discussionboard_members) via foreign keys, and is referenced by posts. 
Special behaviors: Only thread creators or moderators/admins may edit/delete; status may be updated by system or moderation actions.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each thread.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_board_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged board's {@link discussionboard_boards.id}. Thread is attached to a specific board or category.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Creator's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Indicates which member started this thread.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Thread title - Implements requirement for descriptive, searchable topics. Must be unique within the board to prevent confusion. E.g., "Political Reform 2025: National Dialogue". Ensures normalization by storing only atomic string data.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Thread description/body - Implements the need for detailed context. Business meaning: Introductory explanation; markdown supported. Ensures normalization by having one plain text field per thread.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Thread status - Implements business process control (e.g., 'open', 'closed', 'locked'). Used by moderators/admins to control discussion activity.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Thread creation timestamp. Required for audit and ordering. 3NF compliance by storing time info only in this field.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Thread update timestamp, maintained on edits. 3NF compliant.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Thread deletion/soft-delete timestamp. Nullable - only set if thread is deleted, keeps the data for retention/audit trail.

models.name: discussionboard_posts
models.description:
Discussion Post entity - Implements the core requirement for contributions within threads (see 04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md, 2.3). Business purpose: Individual user posts, representing the main argument/content, within a given thread.

Each post is linked to a parent thread and the creating member, without duplicating thread or user information, thus maintaining strict normalization. E.g., a user expresses their view or arguments on a thread topic via a post.

Key relationships: Links to discussionboard_threads (the topic context) and discussionboard_members (the writer). Referenced by discussionboard_comments. 
Special behaviors: Can be edited/deleted by author or moderation subject to business rules.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each post.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_thread_id
foreignFields.description: Parent thread's {@link discussionboard_threads.id}. Defines which thread the post belongs to.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Author member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Who wrote this post.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Main post content/body. Supports markdown for formatting. 3NF: Only pure text; no embedded member or thread info.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Post creation time, for ordering and audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update time, maintained on edits.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp. If null, post is visible; if set, post is deleted but retained for audit/legal purposes.

models.name: discussionboard_comments
models.description:
Discussion Comment entity - Implements the requirement for threaded discussion under posts (see 04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md, 2.3, 2.4). Business purpose: Enables replies to posts to enable in-depth discourse. 

Each comment references its parent post and (optionally) a parent comment (for nested replies). Maintains 3NF by referencing posts/members and storing only one level of content per field. For example, a user responds to a post or another user's argument.

Key relationships: Belongs to a post, created by a member. May link to a parent comment via foreign key (used for threading).
Special behaviors: Deletion is by setting deleted_at; edits update updated_at.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each comment.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_post_id
foreignFields.description: Parent post's {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. Indicates which post the comment belongs to.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Comment author's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Who wrote the comment.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Parent comment's {@link discussionboard_comments.id}. Enables threaded/nested replies. Nullable: only set for replies, not top-level comments.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Comment text/content. Business meaning: User's reply or discussion contribution. Normalized by storing only the text.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Comment creation time. Used for ordering, audit, and display.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Comment last update timestamp. Updated on edits for audit trail.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp. Preserves audit trail on deletion. Null if comment is still live.

models.name: discussionboard_comment_replies
models.description:
Discussion Comment Reply entity (shallow reply index) - Implements explicit requirement for efficiently tracking direct comment replies (see 04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md, discussion flows and threaded conversations).

This table maintains a normalized, junction-like mapping between comments and their direct replies. Useful for fast queries and enforcing reply relationships without embedding reply structure in-line. For example, every reply to a comment generates a row here, which can be traversed for building reply trees.

Key relationships: Both fields are foreign keys to discussionboard_comments. No duplication of content, ensuring 3NF.
Special behaviors: Deletion is handled via the referenced comment's own deletion marker.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each comment-reply relationship.

foreignFields.name: comment_id
foreignFields.description: The parent comment {@link discussionboard_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: reply_id
foreignFields.description: The direct reply comment {@link discussionboard_comments.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Reply relationship creation time. For audit trail and fast reply tree building.

models.name: discussionboard_post_attachments
models.description:
Discussion Post Attachment entity - Implements the need for posts to include attached files (04_DiscussionBoard_Requirements_and_Business_Rules.md, 2.3). Maintains normalized separation between a post and its files.

For example, a PDF, image, or spreadsheet attached to a discussion post. This keeps document/file metadata atomic and notifies the upload pipeline.

Key relationships: Linked to a discussionboard_post, and references file storage/URI.
Special behaviors: Deletions remove only the attachment, not the post.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each attachment.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_post_id
foreignFields.description: Parent post's {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. The post this attachment belongs to.

plainFields.name: file_uri
plainFields.description: Attachment file URI/location. Stores where the file is retrievable (S3, static hosting, etc.). Ensures normalization by keeping only the pointer, not embedded file.

plainFields.name: file_name
plainFields.description: Display name of the attachment file. For user readability and identification; atomic text field per file.

plainFields.name: file_type
plainFields.description: Attachment file MIME type (e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf'). Used to display/hide/preview accordingly. Business meaning: file type constraints and display logic.

plainFields.name: uploaded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was uploaded. Enables audit/control flow.

plainFields.name: uploaded_by
plainFields.description: Uploader's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Member that uploaded the file. Not a foreign key but value is a UUID.

models.name: discussionboard_post_likes
models.description: Stores each instance of a member liking a post. Implements Interaction requirement 2.1, which enables users to upvote/like posts for engagement and reputation calculations. Ensures full normalization (3NF) as this table only contains atomic data about the actor and the action, with all relationships explicit and no calculations or denormalization. Used whenever a member clicks 'like' on a post; supports trending features and user feedback mechanisms. Key relationships: references posts and members (already existing); unique on (post, member) to prevent duplicate likes; deletion cascades if the post or member is removed. Special: soft deletion not required, as unliking deletes the row.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each like entry.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_post_id
foreignFields.description: Target post's {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. Links the like to a specific post.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Liking member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Identifies who liked the post.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the like was recorded. For audit logging and activity timelines. Implements reporting/audit requirements.

models.name: discussionboard_post_dislikes
models.description: Stores each instance of a member disliking a post. Implements Interaction requirement 2.1 and 2.4, supporting user expression and automating moderation signals. Fully normalized (3NF) – atomic event of a dislike, with member and post identity, no calculations. Used when a member clicks 'dislike' on a post; feeds into moderation workflows. Key relationships: references to posts and members (already existing). Unique on (post, member) – one dislike per member per post. Special: row deleted if member cancels dislike.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each dislike entry.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_post_id
foreignFields.description: Target post's {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. Connects dislike to post.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Disliking member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the dislike was made. Supports activity logs and reporting. Requirement: audit trail.

models.name: discussionboard_comment_likes
models.description: Tracks member likes for each comment. Implements Engagement requirements (2.1) for feedback on comment quality and interaction patterns. 3NF enforced: only references comment and actor, with no non-key dependencies. Example: Used to highlight 'popular' comments or calculate feedback scores. Key relationships: references comments and members. Each member may like a comment once (unique composite key). Deleting a comment/member removes likes. No denormalization.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each comment like.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Target comment's {@link discussionboard_comments.id}. Connects like to comment.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member's {@link discussionboard_members.id} who liked this comment.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this comment like was added. Required for activity logs and analysis.

models.name: discussionboard_comment_dislikes
models.description: Tracks member dislikes for each comment. Implements Engagement and Community Health requirements, enabling members to indicate problematic comments and feeding into moderation if thresholds surpassed. 3NF assured: each record is atomic and relates solely to a discrete user action and its object. Example: Used in triggering auto-flagging of comments. Uniqueness constraint prevents multiple dislikes by same member per comment. Connected to comments and members; row deleted if action undone.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each comment dislike.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Target comment's {@link discussionboard_comments.id}. Connects dislike to comment.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Disliking member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of comment dislike event. Supports moderation and audit logs.

models.name: discussionboard_post_reports
models.description: Tracks when a member reports a post as inappropriate/spam. Implements functional and business rules (see sections 2.5, 4 in requirements), providing critical audit, moderation, and abuse detection. Fully normalized structure; all aggregates handled in reporting. Used to initiate moderation against a post, with links to member, post, and reason. Example: member flags a post for hate speech. Uniqueness constraint: one report per member per post. Key relationships: posts and members. Soft/hard deletes as per moderation outcome.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique for each report instance.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_post_id
foreignFields.description: Flagged post's {@link discussionboard_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reporting member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Human-readable reason for report (profanity, spam, etc.). Ensures normalization (atomic string data), no categorization here (handled elsewhere).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report is made. Required for reporting flow and moderation traceability.

models.name: discussionboard_comment_reports
models.description: Tracks each time a member reports a comment as abusive/inappropriate. Implements moderation trigger requirements (sections 2.5, 4), audit logging, and rate-limiting enforcement. Strictly normalized (3NF), atomic event reference. Key relationships: attached to comment and member, no non-key attributes. One report per member per comment (unique composite key). Used for rate-limiting and moderation response automation. Example: 'report' on an offensive comment.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each comment report.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reported comment's {@link discussionboard_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reporting member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for reporting the comment. Worksheets atomic requirement (normalized text, not categorical/aggregated).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of report event; required for traceability (enterprise and legal purposes).

models.name: discussionboard_tag_proposals
models.description: Tracks proposals for new topic tags, per business rule 4. Members propose tags awaiting moderator/admin review; supports platform curation, anti-abuse, and community-driven structure. Complies with 3NF: atomic proposal event, linked to actor (member), no state duplication. Example: member submits new tag 'economic-inequality'. Moderator resolves outside this table. One unique proposal per member/content/tag combo enforced. Relationships: member (who proposed), tag (proposed string), created_at. Special behaviors: tag field is plain string (proposed, not yet accepted).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each tag proposal.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member's {@link discussionboard_members.id} who proposed new tag.

plainFields.name: proposed_tag
plainFields.description: Proposed topic tag string. Enforces normalization (atomic text), not categorized (categorization is result of moderation).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of tag proposal. Used for workflow, audit, and process automation.

models.name: discussionboard_reports
models.description: Report entity - Implements the 'Moderation Reporting' requirement in the requirements analysis. This table tracks all member-initiated reports against posts/comments, ensuring normalized audit trails. For example, it records when a member reports a comment for abuse. Key relationships: reported_by_member_id and resolved_by_moderator_id both reference actors in the system. Special behaviors: maintains clear normalization, no denormalized status/actions.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each report.

foreignFields.name: reported_by_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member's {@link discussionboard_members.id} who reported the content.

foreignFields.name: resolved_by_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator's {@link discussionboard_moderators.id} who resolved this report (nullable if not resolved or auto-resolved).

plainFields.name: target_post_id
plainFields.description: ID of reported post; only set if reporting a post. For normalization: one of post or comment must be filled, never both.

plainFields.name: target_comment_id
plainFields.description: ID of reported comment; only set if reporting a comment. For normalization: at least one of post or comment must be filled, never both.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason or message explaining the report. Atomic value to ensure normalization. For example, 'Spam' or 'Offensive language'.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Workflow status (e.g. 'pending', 'reviewed', 'actioned', 'dismissed'), enabling state-based moderator/automation tracking. Atomic string for normalization.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the report was created. Required for audit.

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: When the report was resolved. Null if unresolved.

models.name: discussionboard_moderation_logs
models.description: Moderation audit log - Implements the audit trail logging requirement, recording every moderator/admin action. Maintains normalized references to users, posts, comments, and detailed action descriptions. For example, logs when a moderator deletes a post. Key relationships: references moderator and affected entity (post/member/comment). Immutable records for compliance and user trust.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies a moderation log event.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator's {@link discussionboard_moderators.id} who performed the logged moderation action.

plainFields.name: target_member_id
plainFields.description: ID of affected member, if action was user-targeted. Nullable for content-only actions.

plainFields.name: target_post_id
plainFields.description: ID of affected post, if any. Null otherwise. Follows 3NF.

plainFields.name: target_comment_id
plainFields.description: ID of affected comment, if any. Null otherwise. Follows 3NF.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Normalized code describing the moderation action (e.g. 'deleted_post', 'suspended_user'). Required for consistent audit analysis.

plainFields.name: action_details
plainFields.description: Freeform message for context/explanation of action. Maintains normalization by storing details, not computed fields.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the moderation action took place. Required for time-based audits.

models.name: discussionboard_suspension_records
models.description: Suspension record - Implements the 'User Suspension' business rule, recording member suspensions (who, when, duration, revoked, etc) for audit and policy enforcement. Each record ties to the member, issuing moderator, and optionally, the revocation event. Clear normalization and referential integrity is enforced. Used by backend to enforce site restrictions on suspended users.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Identifies each suspension event.

foreignFields.name: suspended_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member's {@link discussionboard_members.id} who is suspended.

foreignFields.name: issued_by_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator/admin's {@link discussionboard_moderators.id} issuing the suspension.

plainFields.name: start_at
plainFields.description: Start time of suspension. Not nullable. For audit and enforcement logic.

plainFields.name: end_at
plainFields.description: End time; null if permanent.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Moderator's reason for suspension, atomic string field. For example, 'Multiple code of conduct violations'.

plainFields.name: revoked
plainFields.description: True if the suspension has been formally revoked/freed before end_at. Supports workflow around appeal and moderation audit.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the record was created.

plainFields.name: revoked_at
plainFields.description: If revoked, when the suspension was ended early. Nullable.

models.name: discussionboard_warning_records
models.description: Warning record - Table for warnings issued to members. Implements 'Warnings and Escalations' from business rules. Tracks member, issuer, timestamp and detailed warning message. 3NF maintained: atomic fields, referenced users. Provides historical audit for escalation (multiple warnings before suspension) in normalization-compliant structure.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Identifies each warning issued.

foreignFields.name: warned_member_id
foreignFields.description: Warned member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}.

foreignFields.name: issued_by_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator's {@link discussionboard_moderators.id} who gave the warning.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Flexible string reason or warning details. For example, '1st warning for inappropriate language.'

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of warning action.

models.name: discussionboard_content_flags
models.description: Content flag - Records system or moderator flags on threads/posts/comments for filtering, abuse detection or moderation queues. Implements 'Automated & Manual Flagging' requirement in requirements analysis. Fully normalized; foreign keys for user/content sources, atomic flag attributes. Used to queue content for moderator review or for auto-hide. Key relationships: references flagged post/comment and flag setter (by member or moderator).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for each flagged content event.

foreignFields.name: flagged_post_id
foreignFields.description: Flagged post's {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. Nullable if flag set on comment only.

foreignFields.name: flagged_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Flagged comment's {@link discussionboard_comments.id}. Nullable if flag set for post only.

foreignFields.name: flagged_by_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member's {@link discussionboard_members.id} if the flag was set manually. Nullable for automated/system flags.

foreignFields.name: set_by_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator's {@link discussionboard_moderators.id} if the flag was set by a moderator. Nullable for automated/user flags.

plainFields.name: flag_type
plainFields.description: Atomic string code (e.g. 'spam', 'profanity', 'abuse') indicating flag reason.

plainFields.name: flagged_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when flag was applied. Used for queue/audit compliance.

plainFields.name: auto_flagged
plainFields.description: True if the flag was set by system/automation (not a user or moderator). Maintains workflow clarity.

models.name: discussionboard_notifications
models.description: Discussion Board Notification - Implements the notification delivery and logging requirement as detailed in the Requirements and Business Rules document. This model stores every notification event, such as a reply, mention, moderation update, or announcement, ensuring both reliable delivery and audit trail. Business purpose: accurately targets member accounts and tracks delivery/read states. Maintains strict 3NF normalization; each notification event is atomic, referring to exactly one recipient. Usage examples: generating member notification lists, marking messages as read, auditing notification delivery timelines. Key relationships: references discussionboard_members. Special behaviors: notification records are immutable and individually timestamped for delivery and read receipts.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies the notification record.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Recipient member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. References the user who receives this notification. Maintains referential integrity and supports targeted delivery.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Notification type, e.g. 'reply', 'mention', 'moderation', 'announcement'. Ensures atomic, categorical classification and supports filtering. Example: 'comment_reply', 'moderator_notice'.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Notification title/subject. Briefly summarizes the event. Example: 'You've received a new comment reply.'

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Main content of the notification. Full textual message (e.g., 'Alice replied to your comment ...'). Normalized so that each field is atomic.

plainFields.name: url
plainFields.description: URL to take the user directly to the relevant thread/post/moderation record. Atomic, optional field only present if the notification involves a direct link.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the notification was delivered. Must be filled at the time of sending for traceability.

plainFields.name: read_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating when the user read the notification. Nullable if unread.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When notification record was created. Used for robust audit trails and business intelligence.

models.name: discussionboard_member_notification_settings
models.description: Discussion Board Member Notification Settings - Implements members' personalized notification delivery settings as described in user journeys and requirements. Each record holds a member's per-channel and per-type notification preferences, supporting full normalization and a single row per user. Ensures no redundant or derived data. Typical use: allows members to mute certain notification types/channels while leaving others active. Key relationships: unique 1:1 with discussionboard_members. Special behaviors: one record per member; nullable only for updated_at if not yet updated. Used for programmatically querying or modifying user preferences.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies the settings record.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Foreign key to the user's account. Enforces 1:1 mapping for user preference storage.

plainFields.name: in_app_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether in-app notifications are enabled for this member. Used for quick delivery flag checks. Example: true for active, false for muted in-app alerts.

plainFields.name: email_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether email notifications are enabled for this member. Ensures atomic tracking and filtering by delivery channel.

plainFields.name: reply_notification_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether to alert for replies to the member's content. Each flag is atomic, representing a unique notification scenario.

plainFields.name: mention_notification_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether to alert when the member is @mentioned. Stored atomically and normalized from other notification preferences.

plainFields.name: moderation_notification_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether moderation alerts (actions, warnings, suspensions) are enabled for this user. Supports opt-out privacy/business use cases.

plainFields.name: announcement_notification_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether board-wide announcements should be pushed to this user. Complies with business requirement for member-driven preference control.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this preference record was created. For compliance and audit trail integrity.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this preference record was last updated. Accurate for reviewing user setting changes over time.
